findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) are compared and logged against replay event timestamps (milliseconds)
findings.body:
`fetch_error_details` takes `timestamp` straight from the nodestore event payload, which is in seconds since epoch (~1.7e9). `gen_request_data` (lines 153-155) then compares it with the rrweb replay event's top-level `timestamp`. The replay SDK emits that value in milliseconds (~1.7e12), and `as_log_message` prints the same value.

As a result, every error is "earlier" than the first breadcrumb. All errors are emitted at the start of the log instead of being interleaved in chronological order. The LLM also receives error times and breadcrumb times on different scales.

The unit test and `test_get_with_error` only pass because they use seconds for both values. Convert the error timestamp to milliseconds (e.g. `* 1000`) before comparing and logging.

findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes get_multi preserves order and returns every key
findings.body:
`nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id. It deduplicates ids, returns uncached items first and then cached ones, and omits ids that are not found on some backends.

Zipping the original `error_ids` list with `events.values()` can therefore pair an event id with another event's data. Results are also silently truncated or shifted when some ids are missing or duplicated.

Iterate over `zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and look up `events.get(node_id)` instead. Separately, `node_ids` are built with the replay's own `project_id`, so errors linked to the replay from other projects (e.g. backend errors) are never found.

findings.title: Snuba replay query runs even when error context is disabled, and its failure fails the whole summary
findings.body:
`query_replay_instance` is called unconditionally before the `enable_error_context` check, so `enable_error_context=false` still pays for a Snuba query whose result is thrown away.

In addition, unlike `fetch_error_details`, this query is not wrapped in error handling. A Snuba failure or rate limit therefore turns the optional error-context enrichment into a 500 for the entire summarize request.

Move the query inside the `else` branch and treat its failure as "no error context".

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES are only hidden while a search query is entered
findings.body:
The early return `if (!searchQuery.trim()) return sorted;` runs before the `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` filter. In the default view with an empty search box, `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are still displayed. They only disappear once the user types a search.

Apply the hidden-attributes filter before the early return so it covers both cases.

findings.title: Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization renders with hardcoded empty columns and data
findings.body:
When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the table widget renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`. It ignores `result.data`, `result.meta`, the loading state and field aliases.

Any organization with the flag enabled sees every table widget as an empty table. Wire `result` into `tableData`/`columns`, or keep the flag off until the wiring exists.

findings.title: Assemble analytics event recorded before feature check and validation
findings.body:
`analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` fires before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before schema validation. Requests that end in 404 (feature disabled) or 400 (invalid body) are still counted as assemble events, which inflates the metric.

Recording after the feature check, or after successful validation, would make the event reflect actual assemble attempts.

findings.title: React Query key for attribute keys omits the organization
findings.body:
The new cache key is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`. `queryOptions` contains only itemType, attributeType, project ids, substring and datetime, not the organization slug.

When the project selection is empty (all projects / my projects), two organizations produce identical keys. Cached attributes from one org can then be served for another after switching orgs.

The previous `useApiQuery` key included the org-scoped URL. Add `organization.slug` to the key.

findings.title: Per-issue get_recommended_event() adds N extra Snuba/nodestore lookups per PR comment; titles inserted unescaped into link text
findings.body:
`get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` once per issue when building the merged-PR comment. Each call runs its own Snuba query plus a nodestore fetch, all just to read an environment name; the `Group` row may already carry enough information to avoid this.

Separately, the truncated issue title is now placed inside markdown link text (`[**{title}**]({url})`) without escaping. Titles containing unbalanced `[`/`]` break the link. This includes balanced pairs that become unbalanced after the 50-character truncation.

findings.title: Removed overflow constraint lets long attachment names blow out the table column
findings.body:
The removed `FlexCenter` applied `overflowEllipsis`, which includes `overflow: hidden`. That made the grid item's automatic minimum width 0, so `Name` could truncate within the `1fr` column.

The replacement `<Flex align="center">` has visible overflow. The grid item's min-content width is now the full nowrap file name, so long attachment names expand the column and push Size/Actions out instead of truncating.

Add `min-width: 0` or `overflow: hidden` to the wrapper.

findings.title: FlexBox replacement drops `height: 100%`
findings.body:
The removed `FlexBox` styled component set `display:flex; flex-grow:1; flex-direction:column; height:100%`. The replacement `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>` does not set `height: 100%`.

If the parent is not itself a flex container, `flex={1}` has no effect. The waterfall container can then collapse to its content height instead of filling the available space.

findings.title: Flex replacement loses align-items:center and gap
findings.body:
The old `Container` extended `FlexBox`, so it had `align-items: center; gap: space(1)` plus `justify-content: space-between`. The replacement `<Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between">` drops both alignment and gap. The tabs and vitals are no longer vertically centered or spaced.

Similarly, the second placeholder group at line 27 (`<Flex>`) lost its `align-items: center` and `gap`, so the three placeholders now render touching each other.

findings.title: None max_segment_id case is not actually exercised
findings.body:
The row's `max_segment_id` was changed to `None` to cover the new early-return in `_make_recording_filenames`. However, this test patches `delete_matched_rows`, so `_make_recording_filenames` is never called and the new branch has no coverage.

The pre-fix crash (`range(None + 1)`) would also not have been caught here. Add a direct unit test for `_make_recording_filenames`/`delete_matched_rows` with `max_segment_id=None`.

findings.title: Mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness, so age=0 or timestamp=0 bypass them
findings.body:
`validate_timestamp` rejects only when `self.initial_data.get("age")` is truthy, and `validate_age` only when `timestamp` is truthy. `age: 0` (a valid value for a just-generated report) and `timestamp: 0` (allowed by `min_value=0`) are falsy. A report containing both fields therefore passes validation.

Use `"age" in self.initial_data` / `"timestamp" in self.initial_data`. Also note that a report with neither field is accepted, which contradicts the docstrings saying one must be present.

findings.title: Tests no longer exercise the application/reports+json content type
findings.body:
The previous tests posted with `content_type="application/reports+json"`, the media type browsers actually send. The rewritten success tests post with the default (JSON) content type.

No test now covers `BrowserReportsJSONParser`, so a regression in parsing real browser submissions would go unnoticed. Keep at least one success-path test using `application/reports+json`.

findings.title: Shows 'Project not found' while the projects store is still loading
findings.body:
`useProjectFromId` returns `undefined` until the projects store has loaded. The new check `if (replayRecord?.project_id && !project)` runs before the loading check. When projects are not yet loaded, the tab renders an error alert instead of a loading indicator, even though the project exists.

Gate this error on the projects having finished loading.
